Overview
We are a holding company incorporated in the State of Nevada. In April 2026, we acquired 100% of equity interests of Acellent Technologies (Hong Kong) Co. Limited (“Acellent”), which develops and operates the FinTruth Financial Verification Agent Platform (“FinTruth”), an enterprise AI financial verification platform designed to compare and verify financial analysis and AI-generated financial content against underlying source documents and financial rules, and to produce source-traceable and auditable results. In December 2025 and June 2026, respectively, we sold Advanced Biomed HK (together with its subsidiary, Shanghai Sglcell) and Advanced Biomed Taiwan, thereby disposing of our biomedical operations, and have since fully shifted our focus towards developing our AI application through FinTruth.
Prior to our shift to developing our AI application through FinTruth, we were focused on developing lab devices and chemicals in order to find and study cancer cells in a patient’s blood, with the eventual goal of helping doctors detect and monitor cancer through simple blood tests. Our products included A+Pre, a device that prepares blood samples for testing; the AC-1000, a device that separates cancer cells from the rest of the blood; the A+SCDrop, a device that isolates individual cells; and the A+CellScan, a device that stains and automatically counts cancer cells. We also developed dye kits used to identify different types of cancer cells. With the exception of the A+Pre and AC-1000 devices, most of our products were awaiting regulatory approval from the PRC government. As of the date of this Report, we have terminated our biomedical business and stopped all research in the biomedical field, product development, regulatory approval efforts, manufacturing and sales activities related to our lab devices and their operating chips, and lab chemicals for cancer research purposes.
Our shift to becoming an AI financial verification company is driven by what we believe are the following key drivers of demand for AI financial verification: (1) the wide use of large language models and AI agents by financial institutions in credit analysis, investment research, risk assessment and compliance review; (2) the risk that AI output contains errors from fabricated or miscalculated figures, confused entities, incorrect dates for event sequences, logical contradictions, incorrect policy or regulation citations, and overly optimistic or pessimistic assessments which in turn can lead to poor rating inaccuracies, poor credit decisions, compliance and legal risk; (3) increasing regulatory focus on the explainability, accountability, and accuracy of AI used by regulated financial institutions; and (4) audit and internal-control requirements for documented review and audit trails of the analysis used in decisions and disclosures.
The market for AI verification remains at an early stage, and adoption will depend on financial institutions’ technology budgets, regulatory requirements, model performance, integration costs, data availability and users’ willingness to add automated verification to existing workflows. As such, since our transition from a business focused on biomedical operations to a technology company focused primarily on enterprise AI applications, we have shifted our focus to financial verification and other professional, regulated-use cases. Our AI technology operations currently include: (a) continued development and operation of FinTruth; (b) development of financial verification algorithms, financial rules and related data and knowledge infrastructure; (c) product and software engineering; (d) enterprise product testing, deployment and customer implementation; (e) discussions, demonstrations and commercial engagement with prospective financial-institution and technology customers; and (f) development of commercial models including enterprise subscriptions, usage-based application programming interface (“API”) fees and integrated solutions.
Following the disposition of our biomedical operations, we have maintained a lean, technology-focused operating structure, with personnel primarily engaged in AI research and algorithm engineering, product and software engineering, data and knowledge engineering, customer implementation and commercialization, supported by the finance, legal and corporate functions necessary for a Nasdaq-listed company. We currently do not own any data centers, and the SaaS version of FinTruth runs on rented infrastructure from multiple international public cloud providers. On-premises deployments of FinTruth run on the customer’s own infrastructure. We are subject to the Hong Kong Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance. For on-premises deployments, customer data remains within the customer’s own environment and is subject to the customer’s security controls.
Our objective is to develop recurring and usage-based enterprise revenue from our AI technology operations while maintaining an operating structure in which product development, hiring and commercial expansion are aligned with customer adoption, revenue generation and available financial resources. As such, we are actively engaging in discussions regarding product deployment, business models and pricing with prospective customers and strategic partners, including financial IT companies, MaaS and AI distribution platforms, and fintech subsidiaries of large financial institutions. Target customers include commercial banks, securities firms, insurance companies, asset managers, auditing and professional-services firms, and financial technology companies.
During the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, we generated approximately $127,637 (HK$1,000,000) in revenue from our operations related to FinTruth. We expect to finance the continued operation and commercialization of FinTruth through a combination of operating revenues, proceeds from the disposition of Advanced Biomed Inc. (Taiwan), and future capital-raising activities.
Recent Developments
The ELOC Agreement and the Termination thereof . On June 6, 2025, we entered into a purchase agreement (the “ELOC Agreement”) with HELENA GLOBAL INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES I LTD. (the “Investor”), pursua nt to which we have the right to issue and sell to the Investor, from time to time as provided therein, and the Investor is obligated to purchase from us, up to Twenty-Five Million United States Dollars ($25,000,000) of our Common Stock, subject to terms and conditions set forth in the ELOC Agreement. On July 23, 2025, we filed with the SEC a registration statement on Form S-1 (File No. 333-288907) to register under the Securities Act an aggregate of up to 40,000,000 shares of our Common Stock, which represents the shares available for issuance under the ELOC Agreement (as defined below). The registration statement was never declared effective. On July 20, 2026, we filed with the SEC an application for the withdrawal of the registration statement pursuant to Rule 477 under the Securities Act, as we determined not to proceed with the offering registered thereunder. No securities were sold under the registration statement. On January 30, 2026, we issued 1,650,710 shares of Common Stock (82,536 shares as adjusted for the Reverse Stock Split) to the Investor as commitment fee shares under the ELOC Agreement, valued at $500,000. On July 14, 2026, we delivered to the Investor a notice of termination of the ELOC Agreement pursuant to Section 11.02(b) thereof, and the ELOC Agreement terminated effective July 21, 2026. No advances were made under the ELOC Agreement prior to its termination.
Disposition of Advanced Biomed HK and Shanghai Sglcell. On December 23, 2025, we entered into a spin-off agreement with Wei Ha Hui, an unrelated third party, pursuant to which we sold 100% of the equity interests of Advanced Biomed HK, which wholly owned Shanghai Sglcell, for a purchase price of US$23,000, determined based on a valuation report commissioned by us. All intellectual property owned by Advanced Biomed HK and Shanghai Sglcell was transferred to the buyer at closing. On January 26, 2026, we entered into a supplemental agreement with Advanced Biomed HK and Wei Ha Hui, pursuant to which Advanced Biomed HK acknowledged that it was indebted to us in the aggregate amount of $6,925,549 and irrevocably agreed to repay such amount in full on or before January 26, 2027.
Nasdaq Compliance. On July 18, 2025, we received a written notification from Nasdaq notifying us that we were not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq rules for continued listing on the Nasdaq, and we were provided 180 calendar days, or until January 14, 2026, to regain compliance. On January 16, 2026, we were notified by Nasdaq that our securities would be scheduled for delisting from the Nasdaq Capital market at the opening of business on January 27, 2026 as our common stock had closed below the minimum $1.00 per share as required by Nasdaq

Investing in our securities involves a high degree of risk. Before making any investment decision, you should consider carefully the following risks and other information in this Report, including our consolidated financial statements and related notes. The risks and uncertainties we describe are not the only ones facing us. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of or that we believe are not material at the time could also materially adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. In any case, the value of our Common Stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment. Please also see the section entitled “Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements.”
Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
We recently transitioned our business strategy, and our future success is uncertain.
During our most recent fiscal year, we discontinued our biotechnology operations and redirected our resources toward the development of our artificial intelligence platform FinTruth. Because our continuing business differs significantly from our historical operations, investors have limited information regarding our ability to successfully execute this strategy.
The transition to an AI-focused business involves substantial risks, including developing a commercially viable platform, obtaining customer acceptance, competing against significantly larger companies, protecting proprietary technology, securing adequate financing, and generating sustainable revenues. There can be no assurance that our new business strategy will be successful.
We have generated limited revenue from our AI-focused operations and may never achieve profitability.
Following the discontinuation of our biotechnology business, our continuing operations are focused primarily on developing our artificial intelligence platform FinTruth. We currently generate no significant revenue from these activities and expect that our future operating results will depend largely upon our ability to successfully commercialize our technology.
Commercialization may require substantial additional investments, strategic partnerships, customer adoption, regulatory compliance, and market acceptance, none of which can be assured.
We may rely on a limited number of third parties for marketing, distribution and revenue, and the loss of or underperformance by any of them could harm our business.
We may rely on financial IT companies, MaaS and AI distribution platforms, foundation-model providers and other strategic technology partners for indirect distribution. Depending on a small number of partners concentrates our risk. If any of these relationships ends, is not renewed on favorable terms or underperforms, or if a partner has financial, operational or reputational problems, our revenue, our sales pipeline and our ability to carry out our business plan could be materially and adversely affected.
We have recently transitioned our business to enterprise AI applications and have a limited operating history in this industry, which makes it difficult to evaluate our prospects.
We acquired Acellent in April 2026 and have since disposed of our biomedical operations and shifted our focus entirely to FinTruth, which is currently our sole product. As of the date of this Report, we have not generated any customer revenue from FinTruth, and our revenue relating to FinTruth has been derived solely from agency service fees. Our business plan depends on converting pilot and proof-of-concept engagements into commercial contracts, achieving our twelve-month deployment and hiring objectives, and developing recurring and usage-based enterprise revenue. We may not achieve these objectives on our anticipated timeline or at all, and our limited operating history in the AI industry makes it difficult to evaluate our business and future prospects.
The market for AI financial verification is new and evolving, and may not develop as we expect.
Our strategy is premised on the continued adoption of large language models and AI agents by financial institutions in credit analysis, investment research, risk assessment and compliance review, and on demand for independent verification of AI-generated output. If financial institutions slow or limit their adoption of AI, if foundation-model providers substantially reduce hallucination and other errors in their models, or if customers prefer to rely on manual review or internal tools, demand for FinTruth may be lower than we anticipate. Commercial banks, insurance companies and other regulated institutions also typically have lengthy procurement, security review and approval processes, which may delay or prevent sales.
The AI industry is intensely competitive and rapidly changing, and we may be unable to compete successfully against larger and better-funded competitors.
We face competition from foundation-model providers that may incorporate verification, citation and fact-checking functions directly into their models, from large technology, data and financial information companies, from financial IT companies, and from other AI start-ups. Many of these competitors have substantially greater financial, technical, data and marketing resources, larger customer bases and broader distribution than we do. Some of the same parties with whom we seek to collaborate, including foundation-model providers and financial IT platforms, may also compete with us. The rapid pace of innovation in AI may render our technology obsolete or require us to make significant investments to remain competitive, which we may be unable to fund.
Evolving laws and regulations relating to AI in the jurisdictions where we or our customers operate could increase our costs, restrict our services or reduce demand for FinTruth.
Governments in many jurisdictions, including the United States at the federal and state levels, the European Union and other markets, have adopted or are considering laws, regulations and guidance governing the development and use of AI, including requirements relating to transparency, explainability, risk management, human oversight, data governance and the use of AI in credit and other consequential decisions. Our customers in regulated financial services may be subject to such requirements and may in turn impose them on us. While increasing regulatory focus on the accountability and accuracy of AI is a driver of our business, new or inconsistent regulatory requirements could require us to change FinTruth, limit the use cases or jurisdictions we can serve, increase our compliance costs and expose us to liability.
